title: Support and feedback
description: Get help with STOA, understand teacher support in the learning path, and contact the team when you need us.
description_informal: Get help with STOA, understand teacher support in the learning path, and contact the team when you need us.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
items: Students learn on the star map and ask their questions in Ask, including homework questions and worksheets.
Parents follow their children's progress, reports, and weak areas in the parent dashboard.
Teachers answer help requests from students under Requests.

problems.title: Report a problem
items: Tell us about broken pages, missing data, confusing screens, or anything that stops you from working.
Include the page you were on, what you expected, and what happened instead.
Never send passwords, access codes, or complete conversations from Ask in a support message.
items_informal: Tell us about broken pages, missing data, confusing screens, or anything that stops you from working.

teacherHelp.title: Teacher help or support?
items: Ask for teacher help when a student needs a real teacher to look at a learning question from Ask.
Contact support when your account, your access, a report, or the app itself is not working.
The status of a teacher help request stays in Ask; everything else belongs in support.

expectations.title: What to expect from STOA
items: STOA focuses on learning help that is reliable and easy to follow, and new features arrive step by step.
If something looks unfinished or unclear, tell us: your message helps us decide what to improve next.
If a problem is blocking a lesson right now, say so in your message so we can look at it first.

contactCard.requestText: Write to us about access problems, errors, questions about a report, or anything you are unsure about.

contactCard.generalText: The same address works for general questions about STOA, parent support, teacher applications, and school partnerships.

onboarding.title: Getting started with STOA
onboarding.description: A short guide for students, parents, and teachers using STOA for the first time.

expectations.title: What to expect
items: STOA explains homework step by step, and a real teacher can step in when an explanation is not enough.
If a page is missing data, looks wrong, or does not work, report it through support and we will look into it.
Every message reaches the STOA team, and your feedback shapes what we improve next.

steps.title: Set your grade
steps.description: Add your grade in your profile so STOA explains things at the right level.

steps.title: Learn on the star map
steps.description: The star map shows all your subjects. Pick a star, work through the lessons in its chapter, and it lights up.

steps.title: Ask when you are stuck
steps.description: Open Ask for a homework question, a concept you do not understand, or a worksheet. If an explanation stays unclear, bring in a teacher from there.

steps.title: Open the parent dashboard
steps.description: The parent dashboard shows every child profile, recent activity, and learning signals at a glance.

steps.title: Review the reports
steps.description: Child reports show progress, strengths, weak areas, and recommended support, without showing private conversations by default.

steps.title: Use support for access problems
steps.description: If a child is missing, a report looks out of date, or you cannot sign in, send us a support request.

steps.title: Watch the request list
steps.description: Requests lists open, in-progress, and resolved student requests waiting for a human answer.

steps.title: Open a request
steps.description: Open a request to see the student question in context, add notes, and choose the next status.

steps.title: Keep the status current
steps.description: Move requests through open, in progress, and resolved so students can see how their request is going.
